title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Django basics, setup, and first project!

questions.question: What does Django’s “batteries‑included” philosophy mean?
options: It comes with many built‑in features for common web development tasks
It only works on specific operating systems
It is designed for mobile apps only
questions.explanation: Django provides many features (authentication, admin, ORM) out of the box, so you don’t need to add them separately.

questions.question: Django is a low‑level framework that forces you to write SQL queries for every database operation.
questions.explanation: False. Django uses an Object‑Relational Mapper (ORM) so you can work with databases using Python objects.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a virtual environment?
options: To isolate project dependencies and avoid version conflicts
questions.explanation: Virtual environments create isolated spaces for each project so packages don't interfere with each other.

questions.question: Which command creates a new Django project named `myblog`?
questions.explanation: `django-admin startproject myblog` is the correct command to create a new Django project.

questions.question: What is the role of `manage.py` in a Django project?
options: It contains the main project settings
It is a command‑line utility for project management
questions.explanation: `manage.py` is the central command‑line tool for running development server, creating apps, migrations, etc.

questions.question: The default Django development server runs on port 3000.
questions.explanation: False. The default port is 8000. You can change it by providing a port number after `runserver`.

questions.question: Which file is used to configure database connections in Django?
questions.explanation: Database settings are defined in the `DATABASES` dictionary inside `settings.py`.

questions.question: What does the `startapp` command do?
options: Creates a new Django app inside a project
questions.explanation: `python manage.py startapp <appname>` creates a new app folder with the basic structure for an app.

questions.question: The function used to return a simple HTTP response in Django is `Http________`.
questions.explanation: `HttpResponse` is the class used to return responses (like HTML or text) to the client.

questions.question: A Django project can contain multiple apps, and apps can be reused across different projects.
questions.explanation: True. Apps are designed to be modular and reusable.

questions.question: Which setting must be updated to add a new app to your project?
questions.explanation: You must add the app's name (e.g., `'hello'`) to the `INSTALLED_APPS` list in `settings.py`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `include()` function in `urls.py`?
questions.explanation: `include()` allows you to reference a separate URLconf, typically from an app, to keep URL patterns modular.

questions.question: Django’s development server automatically reloads when you make changes to Python files.
questions.explanation: Yes, the development server watches for changes and restarts automatically – no need to manually restart.

questions.question: Which file is the entry point for WSGI servers (like Gunicorn) to serve a Django application?
questions.explanation: `wsgi.py` is the WSGI entry point used in production by web servers.

questions.question: What command would you use to verify the Django version after installation?
questions.explanation: `python -m django --version` is the standard command. `pip show django` also works, but the question expects the Django command.

questions.question: The `__init__.py` file in a Django folder indicates that the folder is a Python package.
questions.explanation: Yes, it makes the directory importable as a package.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a file created by `startapp`?
questions.explanation: `startapp` does NOT create `urls.py`. You must create it manually if you want app‑specific URL patterns.

questions.question: The `path()` function in `urls.py` takes at least two arguments: the route (URL pattern) and the _____.
questions.explanation: `path()` requires a view (function or class) as the second argument to handle the request.

questions.question: What is the correct way to activate a virtual environment on macOS/Linux?
questions.explanation: On Unix systems, use `source myenv/bin/activate`. On Windows, use `myenv\Scripts\activate`.

questions.question: The `HttpResponse` object can only return HTML content.
questions.explanation: False. It can return any string (HTML, JSON, plain text) by setting the appropriate content type.
